order_note: Predecessor and supersedes SQL 113 (applied to production on 2026-10-23, pin retired): SQL 138 replaces one of SQL 113's six functions, public.aws_public_payee_record(text, text, jsonb), so the engine refuses SQL 138 (predecessors_applied) until SQL 113's objects are at SQL 113's intended state, and after SQL 138 SQL 113 counts as applied only while every other SQL 113 object still matches (staging pin superseded_intended_sha256.sql113, releaseSupersededIntendedHash). The spec prerequisites are public.external_payment_recipients and public.payment_provider_methods with the columns the function reads and writes, SQL 113's aws_public_payee_record(text, text, jsonb) and aws_public_payee_by_token(text) (which it returns through), and role checksops; the file itself raises sql138_prerequisite_missing, sql138_definer_cannot_write or sql138_function_not_owned otherwise. The applying login must be able to write both tables as the function's owner (definer_can_write_relations) and must own the function (functions_owned_by_login); the function must keep its jsonb result (function_results_match) and hold no EXECUTE grant other than checksops and the owner, which the file keeps, and PUBLIC, which it revokes (function_acl_replaceable). Expected production pre-state: the function as SQL 113 left it (release sql138 v1 with SQL 113's body, ec36c29e3472a9777b4a1d08ff7c3da5c00b1dc70cb4b754ef5b04ff0e73633c, derived from SQL 113's bytes by aws/tests/release-sql138-executor.test.mjs and read back on PostgreSQL 16). The change: once verified_at is set, every event through the link (tos_accepted, identity_submitted, bank_linked, bank_verified, any other) returns already_verified and writes nothing; SQL 113's body is otherwise byte for byte the same. aws_public_payee_by_token, aws_payee_create, aws_payee_reissue_link, aws_payee_disconnect and aws_payee_apply_status are not touched. Known API residue (not part of this pin): publicBankAdd in aws/functions/api/providers/payees/handlers.mjs creates the bank account at the payment provider before it calls aws_public_payee_record, so after SQL 138 a leaked link can still attach an unverified extra bank to a verified payee's provider account; the refusal stops the API before its disableBank of the verified bank and the database keeps the verified bank. No API, Lambda or SPA change is part of this pin. Adds no trigger.
